newsitem.title: UK: European markets bask in Wall St's warm glow.
newsitem.headline: European markets bask in Wall St's warm glow.

text.p: European shares took heart from Wall Street's strong close and pushed higher in early trade on Monday, while the dollar softened against the mark as the chance of any early rise in U.S. interest rates receded.

The markets on both sides of the Atlantic were encouraged by the U.S. jobs report for February which on Friday showed little upward pressure on wages, despite a bigger-than-expected rise in the number of new jobs created.
The Dow Jones industrial index closed up 56.19 points at 7,000.89 on Friday having been some 74 points up and U.S. bonds rose, too.
Economists and traders concluded that the jobs report had not given the U.S. Federal Reserve cause to raise interest rates soon to check the threat of inflation.
Any rise in rates could sorely test the global bull market in shares which has pushed valuations to record after record recently.
Investors in shares fear higher interest rates as they harm companies profitability by rising the cost of borrowing. They also make alternative investments more attractive.
By 1100 gmt, London's FTSE index of leading blue chip shares was up 18.6 points, at 4,438.9, while in Paris the CAC-40 index was up 10.15 points at 2,718.43.

Germany's DAX index was up 52.97 points, or 1.57 percent, at 3,429.17, but most of the gains reflected the market, which had closed before Friday's U.S. jobs data, playing catch-up with the gains made elsewhere before the weekend, when London and Paris both closed at new records.
The DAX-Ibis index of electronic trading was up 9.81 points at 3,429.32.
Leading London blue chips shares moved further into record territory, lifted by bullish comments from the Bank of England as well as Wall Street, dealers said.
Gilts also advanced after Bank of England Governor Eddie George said he believed the government could reach its 2.5 percent inflation target this year.

"He raised the question about whether it could be sustained, but up until now, he didn't even think it was a target that could be reached," one London share dealer said of George's forecast. "I think the chance of an early rate increase has receded quite significantly."
Sterling slipped in the wake of George's comments, which was broadly supportive of shares in major exporting companies.
British February producer price inflation was in line with expectations at 1.3 percent and one analyst said the data showed inflation was "very tame at the moment."
In Paris, French shares found support just above the 2,700 level after opening below Friday's record close.
Traders said the market was supported by Wall Street's latest rise and that they expect the U.S. markets to continue climbing.
"The market is consolidating. Wall Street was in good form last Friday," one broker in Paris said.
German shares hit new record highs in early bourse trade with sentiment lifted by Wall Street, firmer bond prices and the stable in slightly lower dollar against the mark.

In currencies, the dollar opened more than a pfennig down against the mark from Friday's close as traders digested the interest rate implications of the U.S. jobs report. It also slipped against the yen.

The dollar received an initial boost on Friday to 34-month highs above 1.72 marks after news of a bigger-than-expected rise in U.S. non-farm jobs but modest hourly earnings data had an opposite influence.

"Late Friday's trade was dominated by unwinding of long dollar positions and the shift in the yield spreads shows shows changes in rate expectations were partly responsible," said Joe Prendergast, foreign exchange strategist at Merrill Lynch.
Chartists said good support is expected at 1.7050, however, and a consolidation above 1.70 marks was the most likely scenario from here as the next batch of U.S. data is awaited.
Elsewhere, the lira retreated from Friday's highs against the mark, hampered mostly by dollar/mark's retreat.

Sterling/mark was also weaker in line with the dollar/mark retreat. Some said the defection of another member of parliament from Britain's ruling Conservative party to the small anti-European Referendumm Party weighed on the pound.
CURRENCIES AT 1100 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.7088 marks and 121.83 yen compared with 1.7182 marks and 121.94 yen in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS 1100 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 18.6 points at 4,438.9.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 10.15 points at 2,718.43.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 52.97 points at 3,429.32 points.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1100 GMT
Gold was quoted at $350.45 an ounce in early European trade compared with $349.05 at the London close on Friday.
